text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- On Tuesday, Parliament passed bills on mortgage funds, earmarking of income tax, and pitbull terriers, and began debating an amendment to the accounting law.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn at his monthly press conference observed that a government that is forced to implement stabilisation measures cannot be popular, although the measures already have yielding results.
- Premiers of countries belonging to the Central European Initiative will meet in Graz, Austria for their regular annual conference on November 8-9.

- Gyula Kovacs, President of the Hungarian Hospitals Federation, warned that unless the hospitals' debts are settled immediately, blood plasmas, infusions and medicines will be depleted in 49 hospitals across Hungary.

- Young Democrat Zoltan Pokorni sought to unleash another privatisation scandal in Parliament yesterday when he alleged that Istvan Korda, portfolio director of the State Privatisation and Holding Co., also president of Antenna Hungaria, wants to transfer ownership of the company to US-based Global Systems Group. Prime Minister Gyula Horn was quoted by Reuters as saying that the privatisation of Antenna is not on the agenda.
- The number of registered unemployed dropped in October as compared to September figures, lowering the unemployment rate to 10.8 percent from September's 11.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. has postponed its decision on the winner of the Magyar Hitel Bank privatisation tender from yesterday to Thursday.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- This paper and Nepszava report that Welfare Minister Gyorgy Szabo tendered his resignation last Wednesday but Prime Minister Gyula Horn refused to accept it.
- A total of $14.2 billion in foreign capital had been invested in Hungary by the middle of this year.
- A commissioner appointed by the culture minister has opened an investigation into a financial scandal in the ministry.
- This paper today prints a lengthy interview with Zsolt Hernadi, the managing director of the soon to be privatised Takarekbank.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said that inflation could drop by 5 percent in each of the next two years, and it could drop below 10 percent by 1999 and 2000 when the crawling peg devaluation could be stopped.

- Sandor Gyurkovics, administrative state secretary at the Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Water, signed a British-Hungarian international public road passenger transportation agreement with John Watts, state minister for public and rail affairs in London Tuesday.
- US-based Global TeleSystems Group has made a proposal to Antenna Hungaria, the state-owned broadcasting company, regarding cooperation on several projects.

- The State Privatisation and Holding Co., has invited a one-round open tender for the purchase of its 77.5 percent stake in the tobacco curing concern Dohanyfermentalo Rt., and has decided to invite a one-round open tender for the purchase of its 77.05 percent stake in the refrigeration company Bekescsabai Hutoipari Rt.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
